title: Club policies, decor and the streetcar gimmick
summary: The club had music five nights a week, no cover, glass-brick decor, and the Claiborne streetcar conductor announced it, filling the place beyond capacity.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And you always had, had music in the hard time?
I already had music, we always kept trill over and we never charge to come in.
I mean six nights a week?
No, yeah, five, yeah, five nights a week. We changed by five nights. We was open, we never did close. We opened from, uh,
No, no, no, five o'clock till one at night. One at night, we was gone. And no cover charge?
No cover charge, never. But how, how were you driving?

Well, our price was pretty high. Everybody said, come to the organization, say that you have to carry a checkbook to go in there. That's perfect, yes. And of course we had a gimmick with it. We got in with the, conducting on the streetcar, you know, we freeze them off a little. And when they, at that time, they had the Claiborne streetcar instead of the Claiborne bus.
Okay, yeah, the streetcar coming up.

Yeah, the Claiborne's right in the middle of the neutral ground, you see. So when he'd get there, when he would get to Louisiana Avenue in Claiborne, the next stop he would say, General Taylor, you know, next stop General Taylor. And right to your left you see the fabulous hurricane. And he would call, just like a train, call up here, call up on a train, right. And of course we got the business, we had more business than we could take here. We couldn't, we couldn't hold the train. The only thing about it, we'd need a larger place. But during that time, you couldn't buy any lumber. See the lumber's all there, the government had everything on there. Yeah, everything would seal off, you see. So we couldn't make it any bigger. You had to hold what we had. What we used to do, we had a lounge in the front, with some couches that'd sit in there, and people would come in and wait for tables, you know. You and your girlfriend would come in, and we'd just tell you to have a seat at the first table, and then we'd come get you there. That's what you said, but we could have really made more money and better if the place had been bigger. We couldn't buy any lumber.
